about.parrafo1: Hello, I am Iván Molina, a UX/UI designer and front-end developer based in Montevideo, Uruguay. I am interested in design that not only looks good but also works well and, above all, improves the experience of those who use it. I like to understand each project as a learning process, where I can grow, refine my perspective, and gradually approach the professional level I admire.
about.parrafo2: Besides design and programming, I am interested in how we relate as a team. I value clear communication, respect for others' ideas, and creating environments where everyone can contribute their best. I care about working with commitment, staying calm in key moments, and pushing forward with attitude, always building from understanding and collaboration.

modalTimeline.alt1: I.T.I Diploma awarded by the Technological Institute of Informatics, certifying the completion of the high school in Informatics.
modalTimeline.alt2: Front-end Developer Diploma awarded by BIOS, certifying advanced skills in front-end technologies.
modalTimeline.alt3: Digital Designer Diploma specialized in web, awarded by ORT, validating knowledge in digital design.
modalTimeline.alt4: Ongoing training through specialized Udemy courses in React 19, Supabase, Node.js, OAuth authentication, payment integration, full-stack architecture, and modern web application development. Knowledge applied directly to real projects like Wake Up Tracker.

proyecto.cap_descripcion: A renewed web platform that connects fans with their club, offering news, statistics, and updated content in an accessible and easy-to-use environment. This project aims to modernize the club's digital presence and strengthen its community bond.
proyecto.nbc_descripcion: NBC Cargo is a company dedicated to imports by air and sea whose website was very outdated. I developed a new page from scratch with a modern and functional design. The renovation improved the user experience and the company’s digital presence. This made access to their services easier and strengthened their online image.
proyecto.havanna_descripcion: Havanna es una propuesta de e-commerce elegante y atemporal para la venta de relojes de lujo. El rediseño se enfocó en crear una experiencia visual cuidada, con navegación intuitiva y una presentación clara de productos y detalles. El objetivo fue modernizar la presencia digital de la marca, facilitando la exploración y selección de productos para los usuarios.
proyecto.culPadel_descripcion: CulPadel was a final university project where we created a corporate image and a website to book courts and rooms, choose date, shift, and payment method, representing all the provided information.
proyecto.worldGym_descripcion: WorldGym is a project that uses public APIs to provide a dynamic experience where you can create and manage personalized workout routines for beginners and intermediates, save favorite exercises, and customize them according to your needs.
proyecto.sandbox_descripcion: Sandbox is a personal project created as a practice space to develop and test front-end concepts. It serves as a collection of landing pages and experiments where I apply React, hooks, and common patterns used in everyday development.
proyecto.transportes_descripcion: Institutional website developed for Transportes UY, a dump truck, crane and container rental company in Uruguay. The project covered everything from UX/UI design to full development, focused on building trust, attracting clients, and positioning the brand digitally.
proyecto.wakeup_descripcion: Wake Up is a personal tracking web app developed independently, from design to deployment. It allows users to log habits, emotions, and daily scores to discover real patterns about their own lives. The project started as a technical practice and ended up becoming a real tool with registered users.
proyecto.facutrainer_descripcion: Facu Trainer is a full-stack web app for a personal trainer. The admin manages clients, routines and metrics, and each client sees their own routine with sets, reps, weight, rest and a video for every exercise.
proyecto.megastrong_descripcion: MegaStrong is a multi-location management system for a gym with 4 locations, with admin, instructor and client roles. It is in development and is my first TypeScript project. I'm building it with Next.js and Supabase.

proyecto_about.sandbox_pregunta1: What motivated you to create Sandbox?
proyecto_about.sandbox_respuesta1: I wanted an environment where I could apply what I learn without the pressure of a formal project. Sandbox was born as a free space to practice React and build landing pages based on existing ideas.
proyecto_about.sandbox_pregunta2: What are you looking to improve with this project?
proyecto_about.sandbox_respuesta2: Mainly my fluency using hooks like useState and useEffect, structuring components more cleanly, and becoming more confident working with props, states, and conditional rendering.
proyecto_about.sandbox_pregunta3: What does Sandbox represent in your growth as a developer?
proyecto_about.sandbox_respuesta3: It’s an intermediate step between theory and professional work. It allows me to make mistakes, experiment, and refine my front-end style, preparing me for larger and more realistic projects.
proyecto_about.transportes_pregunta1: What was the design and development process like?
proyecto_about.transportes_respuesta1: The project started with design rounds in Figma, presented and validated with the client before moving into development. React and Tailwind were used to build a responsive, fast, and maintainable site.
proyecto_about.transportes_pregunta2: What challenges did the project present?
proyecto_about.transportes_respuesta2: One of the main challenges was organizing content for a company with multiple services, ensuring the site communicates everything without overwhelming the user. SEO work was also done to compete with other companies in the industry.
proyecto_about.transportes_pregunta3: What did you learn from working with a real client?
proyecto_about.transportes_respuesta3: It was the first project where I experienced the full cycle of real work: client communication, design decisions backed by reasoning, and the entire publishing process — domain, hosting, and deployment. I also dove deeper into SEO, Google Search Console, and Analytics, understanding that a good website doesn't end at the code — it ends at how people find it.
proyecto_about.wakeup_pregunta1: What was the design and development process like?
proyecto_about.wakeup_respuesta1: The project was developed entirely independently, from Figma wireframes to deployment on Netlify. It was built using React, Tailwind, Supabase, and TanStack Query, developed iteratively with a strong focus on user experience.
proyecto_about.wakeup_pregunta2: What technical challenges did the project present?
proyecto_about.wakeup_respuesta2: The main challenges were implementing Google OAuth authentication, integrating recurring payments with Mercado Pago, building a plan-based restriction system, and developing an AI assistant that analyzes real user data using Groq and Claude.
proyecto_about.wakeup_pregunta3: What does Wake Up represent in your growth as a developer?
proyecto_about.wakeup_respuesta3: It's the most complete project I've built — not just in code but in product vision. I learned to make architecture decisions, design real user flows, integrate external services, and ship something that real people use. I went from doing exercises to building a product.
proyecto_about.facutrainer_pregunta1: What was the design and development process like?
proyecto_about.facutrainer_respuesta1: One of the key decisions was the data model: I separated EjercicioBase, the exercise library, from EjercicioEnDia, a bridge table that links each exercise to a day of the routine. On top of that I built the app with React, Vite, Supabase, Zustand, TanStack Query and Tailwind, and deployed it on Netlify.
proyecto_about.facutrainer_pregunta2: What technical challenges did the project present?
proyecto_about.facutrainer_respuesta2: Separating EjercicioBase from EjercicioEnDia allows independent metrics per day for the same exercise. Security came on top of that: admin and client roles resolved with the SQL function es_admin(), RLS on 6 tables, and delete cascades with restrict on base exercises, which prevent deleting one while other records depend on it.
proyecto_about.facutrainer_pregunta3: What does Facu Trainer represent in your growth as a developer?
proyecto_about.facutrainer_respuesta3: It is work for a real client and it required me to think of the app as a system: a coherent data model, role-based permissions and a different experience for the admin and for the client.
proyecto_about.megastrong_pregunta1: What is the design and development process like?
proyecto_about.megastrong_respuesta1: The project is in development. I'm building it with Next.js, TypeScript and Supabase, and the data model and role-based permissions are the core of the work.
proyecto_about.megastrong_pregunta2: What technical challenges does the project present?
proyecto_about.megastrong_respuesta2: One challenge is avoiding duplicated exercises across locations: I separated ejercicio_base, which is global, from maquina_sede, which stores the machine number at each location. On top of that come the three roles (admin, instructor and client), routines with their ejercicios_en_rutina, and RLS policies in Supabase.
proyecto_about.megastrong_pregunta3: What does MegaStrong represent in your growth as a developer?
proyecto_about.megastrong_respuesta3: It is my first TypeScript project, so I approach it as a learning process: I'm bringing typing into a system with several roles and relations between tables. It is still in development.
